correctness.rationale: The normalized Fock distribution and differentiated Laguerre generating function give \(\chi_m=e^{-at}L_m(vt)\); Gaussian Fourier inversion yields the exact Wigner-Laguerre profile. For nonpositive v-a the Wigner profile is everywhere nonnegative. For positive v-a, radial substitution gives \(\mathcal N_m=\theta^{m+1}F_m/(1-\theta)^m\). Direct integration of the m=1 disk and m=2 annulus yields the formulas. The logarithmic derivative of N2/N1 is \(1/[\theta(1-\theta)]+\mu_1-\mu_2>2-\sqrt2>0\) for all theta in (0,1/2]. Endpoint signs give one root; the eta-to-theta map is strictly increasing and has maximum 1/[2(nbar+1)], proving all physical cases. Checker independently verified Fock characteristic (36), radial Fourier inversion (40) and volume quadrature (12), not replacing the analytic proof. Limits: ideal single-mode inputs and thermal attenuators, not generic noise.

value.rationale: The evaluated exact phase diagram answers a natural operational comparison: whether a second heralded photon addition increases or decreases the integrated Wigner negativity after realistic attenuation of the same thermal seed. One addition dominates near the shared positivity threshold, while two additions dominate above a single universal crossover only for sufficiently cool seeds; warmer seeds never cross regardless of reservoir occupation. The critical occupation \(0.659032\ldots\) and formula for bath-dependent transmissivity provide a complete quantitative decision boundary for this two-protocol design question. This is not a renaming, a single arbitrary parameter slice, or the already known threshold; it combines two different negativity-domain integrals with a global uniqueness proof. Scope intentionally excludes energy-matched yields and arbitrary higher addition.
